comparison: Both address HSPA2 heterogeneity claims (C2, C26, C27, C71). OpenEval finds these well-supported by multiple methods, rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether subtle differences are biologically meaningful and noting measurement limitations. Major disagreement on interpretation of the same data.

Both address temporal expression pattern (C22-C25). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by qRT-PCR data. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED with no specific concerns raised about expression dynamics. Agreement on this aspect.

Both address correlation between HSPA2 and ICM genes (C6). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes lack of explicit p-values and statistical details. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED without raising specific concerns. Mild agreement, though OpenEval is more cautious about statistical rigor.

Both address knockdown effects on ICM markers (C28-C34). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, praising multiple experimental approaches and consistency. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging straightforward experiments with large sample sizes. Strong agreement. OpenEval also addresses RNA-seq data (C72-C74) which peer reviewers discuss separately in R7.

OpenEval R3 includes RNA-seq claims (C72-C74) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R7 rates these UNCERTAIN, noting RNA-seq results are not adequately included or discussed in manuscript and lack contextualization with prior studies. Disagreement on data presentation adequacy.

Both address lineage tracing experiments (C35-C38, C76). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with appropriate acknowledgment of incomplete penetrance. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, specifically questioning clarity of GFP tracking in 2-cell stage injections. Disagreement on experimental clarity and interpretability.

Both address overexpression experiments (C39-C44). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, viewing negative result as important control. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether overexpression construct is fully validated, suggesting negative result may be technical rather than biological. Significant disagreement on interpretation.

Both address HSPA2-CARM1 interaction (C5, C50-C56). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED by co-IP and multiple lines of evidence, noting mechanism not fully elucidated. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning mechanistic link between interaction and lineage specification, and how expression levels are involved. Both note mechanistic gaps but differ in confidence level.

Both address proteomics data (C77-C81). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to limited sample size (2 replicates in KD group) and lack of orthogonal validation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging multiple validation approaches including proteomics without specific concerns. Disagreement on adequacy of proteomics data.

OpenEval R5 addresses primary conclusion C3 (HSPA2 prevents ICM contribution), rating it SUPPORTED based on lineage tracing. No corresponding isolated peer review evaluation of this specific primary claim, though related experimental concerns appear in peer R4.

OpenEval R7 addresses primary conclusion C4 (overexpression insufficient for ICM fate), rating it SUPPORTED as important negative control. No corresponding isolated peer review evaluation, though related construct validation concerns appear in peer R5.

OpenEval R10 addresses pathway enrichment and mechanistic complexity (C66-C68), rating SUPPORTED. Peer R7 partially overlaps on C66 but focuses on RNA-seq data presentation issues (C72-C74). Limited overlap with different emphases.

OpenEval R11 addresses speculative claims about mechanisms and thresholds (C60-C65), rating UNCERTAIN and noting these are hypotheses lacking direct experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these specific speculative claims.

OpenEval R12 addresses background literature claims (C1, C7-C21, C45-C49, C57-C59, C75), rating SUPPORTED as appropriately cited prior knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation as reviewers focus on novel findings rather than literature context.
